evidence.observation: The activate phase of the demo. It lists gateway agents, computes the members that are not yet loaded, and restores only those missing members via 'wattclaw.team.project.member.update' (lines 220-237), then re-lists and throws if any project agent is still absent (lines 244-249). It returns { project, agents, restored } where restored is true only when the incoming project status is 'archived' (line 254), which is exactly the legality rule the demo asserts: a pending -> activated project is not a restore, and no update is issued for already-loaded agents.

The stop/archival path of the demo. It lists projects (line 138), filters to owned agents when an ownership set is supplied (lines 145-147), and for each project classifies it as terminal-expired (success/failed/fail older than FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS, lines 166-168) or restored-archived-expired (lines 169-171). Projects that are neither are skipped and reported in 'kept' (lines 177-180), so a still-running in_progress project can never be archived. Only qualifying projects are archived via 'wattclaw.team.project.archive' (line 187) and reported in 'archived'.

Normalizes the project member list into a de-duplicated set of non-empty agent ids. The demo uses it to assert the activated agent id set is ['p-demo-manager','p-demo-worker'], and the activation path reuses the same helper to compute which agents must exist before it declares success (line 244).

The event source for the demo. subscribe() forces an immediate publish of both watched files (lines 173-174), which produces 'wattclaw.team.project.updated' for config.json (lines 78-92) and 'wattclaw.team.tasks.updated' for task-list.json (lines 95-107); a missing config.json yields 'wattclaw.team.project.deleted'. Later file changes are debounced (lines 117-124) and de-duplicated by raw content (line 74). unsubscribe()/stop() close the watcher once no clients remain (lines 156-180), which is the demo's stop-emits-nothing assertion.

Resolves a project directory from the mounted data roots using the validated path segments (lines 9-19) and returns the first candidate that exists on disk. The demo calls it to prove the freshly created local fixture lives at the exact tenant-scoped path (tenantId/.wattclaw-team/projects/<projectId>) the runtime expects.

claims.claim: The create phase of a fresh local project fixture emits exactly the WattClaw project events: 'wattclaw.team.project.updated' carrying the pending project and 'wattclaw.team.tasks.updated' carrying the empty task list, addressed to the subscribing client; the fixture directory is resolvable on disk at <root>/<tenantId>/.wattclaw-team/projects/<projectId>.

Activation restores only the genuinely missing members of the project: 'activateWattClawProjectRuntime' issues 'wattclaw.team.project.member.update' once for the unloaded worker and skips the already-loaded lead, returns the full agent id set, and reports restored=false for a pending (non-archived) project.

Only legal lifecycle transitions are taken: the runtime moves created->pending->in_progress->success->archived, and the retention/stop pass refuses the illegal in_progress -> archived transition for a running project (it is returned in 'kept') while archiving the expired terminal success project via 'wattclaw.team.project.archive'.
Stopping the demo (unsubscribe/stop) releases the file watcher so getActiveProjectCount() drops to zero and no further events are emitted for subsequent config.json writes.

conclusion: The demo drives a fresh, dependency-free local WattClaw project fixture through create -> activate -> stop using the shipped modules, and every phase holds: create materializes the fixture and emits project.updated(pending) plus tasks.updated([]); activate restores exactly the one missing agent, leaves the loaded lead untouched, and advances pending -> in_progress with a matching event; stop releases the watcher (no further events) and archives only the expired terminal project while refusing to archive the still-running one. All four observed transitions are members of the asserted legal-transition set, and the three refusal cases (success->in_progress, pending->restored, failed->in_progress) throw as required. The demo script exits 0 (PASS).

validation.notes: Exit code 0. Output: 'WattClaw project lifecycle demo: PASS' with all four phase assertions and the observed transition trace '(created)->pending, pending->in_progress, in_progress->success, success->archived'. The script imports the real server/services modules and uses only Node built-ins, so no install step was needed. Limitation: this repository has no node_modules and no vitest binary installed, so the pre-existing vitest suites (server/services/wattclaw-project-runtime.test.js and wattclaw-project-events.test.js) could not be executed in this environment; the demo reproduces their key scenarios (missing-agent restore, retention archiving) with the dependency-free runner instead.
